title: How Hunger Can Trigger Alcohol Cravings - Nautilus
gist: A Current Biology study finds hunger may trigger alcohol cravings in fruit flies, which researchers hope will inform understanding of cue-driven relapse and addiction treatment in humans.

insights.claim: A new Current Biology study finds that hunger may be involved in triggering alcohol cravings in fruit flies.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Early animal-model evidence linking internal state to addiction cues.
insights.locator: Now, a new study published in Current Biology

insights.claim: Brain processing shifts with internal states such as hunger, thirst or pain, including in animals with simple brains like fruit flies.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Internal-state-dependent processing is relevant to addiction therapeutics.
insights.locator: Our brains process information slightly differently

insights.claim: Fruit flies are useful models because a map of the entire fly brain and many genetic tools exist, and their neural circuitry is simpler.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Simple models allow circuit-level work that precedes human translation.
insights.locator: Why study fruit flies to understand human brains?

insights.claim: Study author Lewis Sherer of Brown University says understanding how flies remember alcohol could hint at how humans link cues to alcohol and how to prevent relapse and treat addiction.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Long-dated translational angle for addiction treatment.
insights.quote: If we can understand at a smaller level how an organism like a fly can remember alcohol, that is a step forward
